title: Jharkhand High Court Quashes Cancellation of JSSC CGL Exam and Appointments
excerpt: Justice Deepak Roshan set aside the government's August 18 cancellation order, restoring appointments for selected candidates while allowing the CID probe into alleged irregularities to continue.
body:
• The Jharkhand High Court on Friday quashed the state government's August 18 order cancelling the JSSC Combined Graduate Level exam and all appointments made through it.
  • Justice Deepak Roshan held that all selected candidates could not be presumed guilty based only on allegations of irregularities, petitioners argued.
  • The CID probe into the alleged exam irregularities will continue, monitored by retired judge Gautam Kumar Choudhary with retired IPS officer R.K. Mallik as nodal officer.
  • For appointed candidates: the interim stay that kept them in service is now backed by a final ruling restoring their appointments; the detailed order is yet to be released.

Court restores the appointments

The Jharkhand High Court has set aside the state government's decision to cancel the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission's (JSSC) Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination and the appointments made on its basis, according to IANS reporting in Hi India. Justice Deepak Roshan delivered the verdict on Friday while hearing petitions filed by successful candidates challenging the government's order.

On August 18, the state government had cancelled the CGL examination, certain other recruitment tests, and the appointments made through them, citing a CID investigation report and protests by aspirants. It later submitted a sealed report to the court claiming the recruitment process was marred by large-scale irregularities and systemic failures.

Why the court rejected a blanket cancellation

The petitioners, including candidate Akash Gaurav, argued that individuals involved in any wrongdoing could be identified and proceeded against separately. They contended it was neither fair nor justified to scrap the entire selection process and invalidate all appointments because of the alleged misconduct of a few candidates.

During the hearings, the court observed that all selected candidates could not be presumed guilty only on the basis of allegations of wrongdoing in the examination process, as reported by IANS and summarised by Town Post.

Timeline and the continuing probe

The High Court had reserved its judgment on October 8 after hearing arguments from all parties. On the same day, it continued its interim stay on the cancellation order, allowing affected employees to remain in service until the final verdict. Earlier, on September 18, the court had appointed retired judge Gautam Kumar Choudhary to monitor the investigation into the alleged irregularities, with retired IPS officer R.K. Mallik designated as nodal officer, and directed that candidates selected through a fair process should not be harassed in the name of the investigation.

Background: a closely watched recruitment test

The JSSC conducts the CGL examination to fill various state government posts, and it is one of Jharkhand's most closely watched recruitment tests, according to Town Post. That scale is why a blanket cancellation mattered so much: it did not affect a handful of applicants, but hundreds of candidates who had already cleared the process and, in many cases, taken up appointments. The August 18 cancellation also covered certain other recruitment tests, and it followed protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities — the same allegations the CID is still investigating under court monitoring.

What happens next

The appointments stand restored, but the CID investigation into the alleged examination scam will continue. The detailed order is yet to be released, and its reasoning should clarify how investigators can pursue individual wrongdoing without overturning the whole selection.
